body_html:
How it works

Simultaneous equations are two equations that are true at the same time. The solution is the one pair of values (x, y) that works in both. It is where the two lines cross.

Elimination: make one letter have the same number in front in both equations. If the signs are different, add. If the signs are the same, subtract. Substitution: if one equation says y = …, put that into the other equation.

Example

Solve 3x + y = 11 and x − y = 1.

Signs differ, so add: 4x = 12, x = 3.

3 − y = 1, so y = 2.

Answer: x = 3, y = 2

Example

Solve 2x + 3y = 12 and x + y = 5.

Multiply the second by 2: 2x + 2y = 10.

Subtract: y = 2, then x = 3.

Answer: x = 3, y = 2

Example

Solve y = 2x and x + y = 9.

x + 2x = 9, so x = 3.

y = 2 × 3 = 6.

Answer: x = 3, y = 6

Common mistakes

  • Adding when you should subtract. Same signs: subtract. Different signs: add.
  • Multiplying only one side of an equation. Multiply every term.
  • Finding x and stopping. You must find y as well.
  • Swapping the values of x and y. Check your answer in both equations.

faq.a: Two equations with two unknowns that are both true at once. The solution is the pair of values that works in both.

faq.q: Do I add or subtract the equations?
faq.a: Look at the letter you want to remove. If its signs are the same, subtract. If they are different, add.
When one equation already says y = … or x = …. Put that expression into the other equation.

faq.q: How do simultaneous equations link to graphs?
faq.a: Each equation is a straight line. The solution is the point where the two lines cross.

items.q: 2 adult tickets and 3 child tickets cost $45.70. 3 adult tickets and 1 child ticket cost $42.30. How much is one adult ticket?
items.e: Let x = one adult ticket and y = one child ticket (in cents): 2x + 3y = 4570 and 3x + y = 4230. Multiply the second by 3 and subtract the first: 7x = 8120, so x = 1160. $11.60.

items.q: 2 coffees and 3 teas cost $11.50. 3 coffees and 1 tea cost $12. How much is one coffee?
items.e: Let x = one coffee and y = one tea (in cents): 2x + 3y = 1150 and 3x + y = 1200. Multiply the second by 3 and subtract the first: 7x = 2450, so x = 350. $3.50.

items.q: 2 pens and 3 pencils cost $4.80. 3 pens and 1 pencil cost $5.10. How much is one pen?
items.e: Let x = one pen and y = one pencil (in cents): 2x + 3y = 480 and 3x + y = 510. Multiply the second by 3 and subtract the first: 7x = 1050, so x = 150. $1.50.

items.q: 2 burgers and 3 drinks cost $14.60. 3 burgers and 1 drink cost $15.60. How much is one burger?
items.e: Let x = one burger and y = one drink (in cents): 2x + 3y = 1460 and 3x + y = 1560. Multiply the second by 3 and subtract the first: 7x = 3220, so x = 460. $4.60.

items.q: 2 notebooks and 3 rulers cost $9.60. 3 notebooks and 1 ruler cost $9.50. How much is one notebook?
items.e: Let x = one notebook and y = one ruler (in cents): 2x + 3y = 960 and 3x + y = 950. Multiply the second by 3 and subtract the first: 7x = 1890, so x = 270. $2.70.

items.q: Two numbers add to 30 and their difference is 8. What are the numbers?
Two numbers add to 50 and their difference is 14. What is the larger number?
items.e: 2x = 50 + 14 = 64, so the larger number is 32.

items.q: The sum of two numbers is 17. Twice the first plus the second is 24. What is the first number?
A farm has hens and cows. There are 20 heads and 56 legs. How many cows are there?
items.e: x + y = 20 and 2x + 4y = 56. Double the first: 2x + 2y = 40. Subtract: 2y = 16, so y = 8 cows.

items.q: At which point do the lines y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 7 cross?
items.e: 2x + 1 = −x + 7, so 3x = 6 and x = 2. Then y = 5. The lines cross at (2, 5).

items.q: At which point do the lines x + y = 10 and y = x + 4 cross?
A theatre sold 200 tickets. Adult tickets cost $12 and child tickets cost $7. The total was $1900. How many adult tickets were sold?
items.e: x + y = 200 and 12x + 7y = 1900. Multiply the first by 7: 7x + 7y = 1400. Subtract: 5x = 500, so x = 100.

items.q: Xin Yi has 25 coins. They are all 10p and 20p coins. They are worth $3.70. How many 20p coins does she have?
items.e: x + y = 25 and 10x + 20y = 370. Multiply the first by 10 and subtract: 10y = 120, so y = 12.

items.q: Which pair of values satisfies both x + y = 9 and x − y = 3?
Marcus solves 2x + y = 9 and x + 3y = 7 and gets x = 4, y = 1. What should he do to check?
items.e: 2(4) + 1 = 9 ✓ and 4 + 3(1) = 7 ✓. Substitute into both equations; the answer must work in each.

In 5 years, Mei Ling will be twice as old as her brother. Now the sum of their ages is 26. How old is Mei Ling now?
How many solutions do x + y = 5 and 2x + 2y = 10 have?
items.e: The second equation is the first multiplied by 2, so they are the same line: infinitely many solutions.

items.q: How many solutions do x + y = 5 and x + y = 8 have?
items.e: x + y cannot be 5 and 8 at the same time. The lines are parallel: no solution.
